title: test: backend unit tests with 95% coverage gate
body:
## Summary
Adds a Jest unit-test suite for the backend and enforces a **95% coverage gate** in CI. The repo previously had **zero tests**; this brings it to **231 tests** with **99.6% line coverage**.

Adapts the "Java Unit Testing (95% Coverage)" playbook to this TypeScript/Node stack: Jest + ts-jest replace JUnit/Maven, and Jest `coverageThreshold` replaces the JaCoCo `check` rule.

**Coverage (all thresholds met):**
```
Statements : 99.63% (830/833)
Branches   : 96.5%  (386/400)   threshold 85%
Functions  : 100%   (116/116)
Lines      : 99.62% (803/806)   threshold 95%
```

**What changed**
- `backend/jest.config.js` — ts-jest preset, `coverageThreshold` global `{ lines: 95, statements: 95, functions: 95, branches: 85 }`, `collectCoverageFrom: src/**` excluding `index.ts`/`*.d.ts`.
- `backend/src/app.ts` (new) — Express app extracted from `index.ts` so Supertest can attach without `app.listen()`; `index.ts` now only bootstraps.
- `backend/test/` — global setup (deterministic env, mocked `dotenv`, silenced console), reusable helpers: chainable+thenable Supabase query-builder mock, Express `Response` double, single-router app factory. Unit tests for every route, middleware, service (`voiceEngine`, `aiOrchestrator`), config and utils. All external boundaries (Supabase, Twilio, OpenAI, `fetch`) are mocked — no real network/DB.
- CI: new `Test backend (95% coverage gate)` step runs `npm run test:coverage`; the job fails if coverage drops below threshold.

**Real defect found & fixed by tests**
`parsePagination` returned `NaN` for non-numeric `page`/`limit` (`Math.max(1, parseInt('abc'))` → `NaN`). Added explicit `Number.isNaN` guards so it falls back to defaults (page 1, limit 25).
